findings: Rejected on one process defect; the mechanism itself survives every held-out case. 221a17da0 adds the high-precision literal 76.6016 (text_render.rs test explicit_font_monospace_decodes_to_dialog, `let mut menlo = base(26.0, 76.6016);`) with no provenance comment and no baseline update. decimal_literal_ratchet at base lists class.rs, deployment.rs, plantuml_metrics.rs and state.rs; at the tip it also lists `crates/rustuml-render/src/text_render.rs: 51 -> 52`. Counts per file with the guard's own rule: text_render.rs 51 at cb550c0d6, 505999cac and 0cd7743aa, 52 at 358b6e285; every other changed file is unchanged. The ratchet is therefore worse than at the merge base (Parity Honesty Rules 3 and 4). The value duplicates the base() argument on line 2025, so the fix is to reuse that binding or compute it, not to fit anything; a re-check needs only harness_guards, the workspace lib tests, and a byte-identical CLI stdout check on CZ, since test code does not reach the binary.

Font.decode port: decoded_font_name follows JDK 21 Font.decode step for step (lastHyphen/lastSpace separator, Integer.valueOf size including non-positive, style token bolditalic|italic|bold|plain, trailing-separator trim, lastIndexOf with a negative fromIndex). Held-out CZ cases that only exercise it all match Java at the tip: name-style-size, name style size, name-bold, name-bolditalic, name-italic-12, numeric-only, trailing dash. The empty name (g3r2_sk_empty) measures correctly (48.7061) but Java writes font-family="''" and Rust writes sans-serif, identically in pre, base and tip.

Family and PostScript table: all 16 REGISTERED_POSTSCRIPT_FACES rows are census.tsv PostScript names whose census family maps to the same MetricFamily and whose bold/italic bits match the name. Every census face of a modelled family that the table omits reduces through Font.decode to a modelled family (Helvetica, Helvetica-Bold, LucidaGrande-Bold, Menlo-Bold, Menlo-BoldItalic, Menlo-Italic, Verdana, Verdana-Bold/-Italic/-BoldItalic) except Helvetica-Light and Helvetica-LightOblique, which have no extracted advances and are declared residue. JDK logical names Dialog, DialogInput, Serif, SansSerif, Monospaced and the CSS spellings monospace, MONOSPACE, serif, sans-serif all match Java at the tip in CZ (monospace, MONOSPACE and Monospaced are tip gains).
